confirmed.claim: "There are no imports, props, or types: reuse occurs through three unconstrained slots and copied class expectations." (challenge-L-library.md:9)
confirmed.proof: TRUE and stronger than stated. /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue is 24 lines of pure <template> with NO <script> block at all (sha256 a15213…c7a matches the corpus receipt, so the audit is against current HEAD). `grep -rL "<script" demo --include="*.vue"` returns exactly ONE file in the whole demo tree — AdminListItem.vue — so it is the sole script-less SFC and a genuine house outlier. Slot names/payloads are declared nowhere: `grep -rn defineSlots demo/` = 0 hits, so slot misuse is invisible to vue-tsc. The only contract is the prose comment at AdminListItem.vue:2-5 ("w-8 h-8 expected", "text-small", "text-caption text-muted-foreground"), which the compiler cannot enforce — and the sole consumer already drifts from it (AdminNamesPanel.vue:52 uses `text-mono-small`, not the comment's `text-caption`). The minimal cure (a `<script setup lang="ts">` with `defineSlots<{swatch?():any; content():any; actions?():any}>()`) is structurally sound and cheap; the corpus's larger prescription is killed separately (L-5).

confirmed.claim: "The row frame is duplicated in `AdminListSkeleton` instead of shared structurally." (challenge-L-library.md:11)
confirmed.proof: TRUE, and the corpus UNDERCOUNTS it. The frame `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge` appears verbatim at THREE sites: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:11, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListSkeleton.vue:9, and /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 (the third is invisible to all three axes). The bare geometry prefix `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5` recurs at two more sites (AdminUsersPanel.vue:80, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:50) — five copies of one grammar in one 8-file directory. The prescribed cure is sound for the skeleton: AdminListSkeleton.vue:13-18 fills exactly the swatch/content/actions zones, so it could consume <AdminListItem> with its three slots and keep its own `skeleton-ink-register`, role="status", aria-label via fallthrough attrs. Divergence has already begun — see the MISSED finding on AdminAuditPanel:62's extra hover/transition.

confirmed.claim: "The root has no `role`, item ID, selected state, disabled state, or keyboard contract." (challenge-C-implementation.md:11)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED IN PART — the `role` limb only; the rest is refuted inside this same proof. Fact: AdminListItem.vue:11 is a bare `<div class="flex items-center …">` with no role, and the sole consumer's list containers (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43 and :93, `<div class="grid gap-2 min-w-0">`) carry no `role="list"` either — so the moderation queue has zero list semantics end to end, while the sibling palette grid DOES (PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`, children `role="article"` at PaletteCard.vue:22). That is a real in-house inconsistency. But the corpus MISLOCATES the cure: `role="listitem"` requires an owning `role="list"` ancestor, so stamping a role on the leaf alone would produce an orphaned listitem — the fix belongs at AdminNamesPanel.vue:43,93, not in AdminListItem. The remaining limbs are refuted: there is no item ID to hold (`:key="item.id"` at AdminNamesPanel.vue:44,94 is Vue-internal), and selected/disabled/keyboard contracts are inventions — no consumer selects, disables, or keyboard-activates a row; all interaction lives in the slotted Buttons (AdminNamesPanel.vue:55-69, 106-114), each with an item-specific aria-label.

confirmed.claim: "The root is a generic `div`, not a list item, article, row, link, or button. Consumers must invent semantics independently." (challenge-D-design.md:11)
confirmed.proof: DUPLICATE OF C-3 — same defect, counted once. Verified at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:11 (bare div) and the consumer that invented nothing (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43,93). The second sentence is the accurate half: the house DOES have the precedent (PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 + PaletteCard.vue:22) and this cluster did not follow it. Same mislocation caveat: the container, not the leaf, is where `role="list"` must land.

confirmed.claim: "Truncation is delegated to content supplied by callers; the wrapper only hides overflow, potentially clipping focus rings or important text." (challenge-C-implementation.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED AS LATENT-ONLY, downgraded to INFO. Both halves check out structurally: truncation is indeed caller-side (`truncate` at AdminNamesPanel.vue:50,52,100,102 — nothing in AdminListItem truncates), and `overflow-hidden` at AdminListItem.vue:17 WILL clip any focus ring, box-shadow, or popover that a future content slot renders, because the clip is on the column itself. But there is no live manifestation: the only content ever slotted is two non-focusable `<span>`s, and each already self-truncates, which makes the parent `overflow-hidden` redundant for the shipping case (it is a defense against a non-truncating caller, not the mechanism). No focusable element has ever been placed in the content slot, so nothing is clipped today. Cite as a latent hazard on the module, not a live defect.

confirmed.claim: "Empty `swatch` and `actions` slots still leave fixed boxes/gaps; there is no conditional rendering." (challenge-C-implementation.md:9; restated at challenge-D-design.md:12)
confirmed.proof: Structurally TRUE, operationally inert. AdminListItem.vue:13 renders `<div class="shrink-0 w-8 h-8 …">` unconditionally, so an empty #swatch still costs 32px + the root's 12px `gap-3`; AdminListItem.vue:20's actions wrapper collapses to 0 width but the flex `gap-3` between items still applies (~12px). There is indeed no `v-if="$slots.swatch"`. However the claim has ZERO live reach: the component has exactly one consumer file (AdminNamesPanel.vue, the only `import AdminListItem` in the tree) with two call sites (:44 and :94), and BOTH supply all three slots (:45-47/:48-53/:54-70 and :95-97/:98-103/:104-115). So this is a latent API-robustness gap, not a rendering defect — INFO, and the corpus's SOURCE-RED weighting of it is unwarranted.

confirmed.claim: "Swatch, content, and actions are visual slots with no labels or required anatomy. Empty slots still reserve space." (challenge-D-design.md:12)
confirmed.proof: DUPLICATE — limb 1 is L-1 (undeclared slots, AdminListItem.vue:1-24 has no script/defineSlots), limb 2 is C-1 (unconditional wrappers at AdminListItem.vue:13,20). Both verified; counted once each above. Recorded here only so the D axis is not credited with an independent find.

killed.claim: "Verdict: SOURCE-RED. The implementation cannot enforce the semantic or layout invariants its comments promise." (challenge-C-implementation.md:5)
killed.refutation: FALSE on the layout half, which is the half the comments actually assert. The one layout invariant the comments promise is the S.W5-12/F-1 cure documented at AdminListItem.vue:6-10 — min-w-0 on the row itself so the content column can truncate — and it IS enforced, at AdminListItem.vue:11 (`min-w-0` on the root grid item) and AdminListItem.vue:17 (`flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-hidden`). The live composition closes the loop: the container is a grid (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43 `grid gap-2 min-w-0`) so the row is genuinely a grid item, and the slotted spans carry `truncate` (AdminNamesPanel.vue:50,52). This is the exact chain that fixed a documented P0 (AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-9: approve/reject pushed ~250px off-card at 390px, moderation INOPERABLE). A verdict asserting the component 'cannot enforce' its layout invariant is contradicted by the working cure sitting on the cited lines. The semantic half survives only in the narrow form confirmed as C-3.

killed.claim: "Verdict: SOURCE-RED. This is a reusable primitive in practice but has no explicit library contract." (challenge-L-library.md:5)
killed.refutation: "Reusable primitive in practice" is refuted by enumeration. `grep -rn AdminListItem demo/` yields exactly one importer — AdminNamesPanel.vue:128 — with two call sites (:44, :94), both rendering identical anatomy. It is not re-exported from the cluster's declared public surface (demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-8 exports the five panels and NOT AdminListItem/AdminListSkeleton/PaginationBar), so it is a deliberately private in-directory leaf, not a library primitive. The whole L-axis frame — and the severity that follows from it — rests on a reuse premise the tree does not support.

killed.claim: "Comments specify an expected 8×8 swatch and typography, but the component neither supplies nor validates those primitives." (challenge-L-library.md:10)
killed.refutation: "Neither supplies" is factually FALSE. AdminListItem.vue:13 supplies precisely that primitive: `<div class="shrink-0 w-8 h-8 flex items-center justify-center">` is a fixed 32×32 centering box the caller's swatch drops into. The component supplies the 8×8 geometry; only *validation* is absent (which is L-1, already confirmed). The corpus in fact has the finding backwards — the real code smell is the OPPOSITE: because the comment at :3 tells callers to also write `w-8 h-8`, the sole consumer duplicates the wrapper's own sizing (AdminNamesPanel.vue:46 and :96, `class="w-8 h-8 rounded-full …"`). See the MISSED finding on that duplication.

killed.claim: "Arbitrary slot content can violate expected dimensions, overflow, or contain nested interactive controls with conflicting row behavior." (challenge-C-implementation.md:10)
killed.refutation: Unfalsifiable as written, and its one testable limb is false. "Conflicting row behavior" presupposes the row HAS behavior: AdminListItem.vue:11 carries no @click, no @keydown, no role, no tabindex — there is nothing for a nested control to conflict with, and no consumer adds any (AdminNamesPanel.vue:44,94 pass only slots). The residual "arbitrary slot content can violate dimensions" is true of every slot in every component ever written and predicts no specific failure; the actual dimension risk (no overflow clip on the fixed swatch box) is concrete and is filed as a MISSED finding rather than credited to this prose. Killed as a non-claim.

killed.claim: "There is no detail/disclosure region even though admin rows often need it; consumers may create detached siblings." (challenge-C-implementation.md:12)
killed.refutation: Speculative requirement-invention, refuted by the tree in both directions. (a) No consumer of AdminListItem needs disclosure: the color-name queue rows are name + CSS literal + approve/reject (AdminNamesPanel.vue:44-71, 94-116) — nothing to disclose. (b) The one admin surface that DOES have a disclosure region does not use AdminListItem at all: AdminUsersPanel.vue:134 hand-rolls its expandable panel under a hand-rolled row (:78-90), so no consumer 'created a detached sibling' of AdminListItem — the predicted harm has zero instances. Adding an unused detail region to a 24-line shell is exactly the contrivance the house forbids (feedback_kiss_no_contrivance: don't build wrappers/regions that don't exist yet).

killed.claim: "The trailing action cluster can grow without a width/overflow policy and can squeeze identity content on phone widths." (challenge-D-design.md:13)
killed.refutation: Mechanism true, defect false, and the prescribed cure would REGRESS a documented P0. Yes, AdminListItem.vue:20 is `shrink-0` while AdminListItem.vue:17 is `flex-1 min-w-0`, so in principle actions win. But live actions are two icon-only buttons at `h-7 px-2` with 3.5-unit icons (AdminNamesPanel.vue:55-69) — roughly 66px including the 6px gap — leaving ~250px of content on a 390px row. More decisively: making the action cluster shrinkable is precisely what the S.W5-12/F-1 work fixed away from. AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-9 records that the failure mode was approve/reject being pushed ~250px OFF-CARD at 390px, and the cure was min-w-0 on the truncatable column while the controls stay unshrinkable. Applying this finding would reopen that regression.

killed.claim: "Hover, focus-within, selected, disabled, destructive, pending, and expanded states have no row-level design." (challenge-D-design.md:14)
killed.refutation: Inverted: row-level states would be a DEFECT here, not a cure. AdminListItem rows are inert containers (no handler/role/tabindex at AdminListItem.vue:11), so a row-level hover or selected treatment would advertise an interaction that does not exist. Every affordance correctly lives on the slotted controls, which do carry full state design — hover/focus-visible destructive ramps at AdminNamesPanel.vue:64 and :109 (`text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive focus-visible:text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10`), the F-8 'ink at rest' rule. The tree also supplies the counter-example that settles it: the ONE admin row that took this advice — AdminAuditPanel.vue:62's `transition-colors duration-fast hover:bg-accent/50` — sits on a div with no click, no keydown, no role and no tabindex (:59-63), i.e. a phantom affordance. Meanwhile AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-90 gates hover strictly on interactivity. The corpus is prescribing the bug.

killed.claim: "The row has a border/radius but no signature connection to the admin information architecture; it risks becoming a generic card repeated everywhere." (challenge-D-design.md:15)
killed.refutation: Refuted by enumeration and self-contradiction. 'Repeated everywhere' = one importer (AdminNamesPanel.vue:128), two call sites, and deliberately withheld from the cluster's public surface (demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts exports only the five panels). It cannot spread: nothing outside the directory can even reach it. The remainder ('no signature connection to the admin information architecture') names no observable property, prescribes no change, and is not falsifiable. Note the corpus also contradicts itself across axes — L-13 argues the pattern is common enough to promote to glass-ui, D-15 warns it is spreading, while the tree shows a single private consumer.

killed.claim: "Action semantics, item semantics, selection, disclosure, and navigation are all delegated, so consumers can produce incompatible or inaccessible rows under the same visual shell." (challenge-L-library.md:12)
killed.refutation: Delegation IS the contract of a layout shell, and the predicted harm has no instances. With one consumer rendering two structurally identical rows (AdminNamesPanel.vue:44-71 vs :94-116 — same swatch, same primary/secondary spans, same button rung), there are no 'incompatible rows' to point at, and the rows that ARE produced are more accessible than most of the tree: every icon-only control carries an item-scoped aria-label (:55, :65, :110) and every icon is aria-hidden (:56, :68, :113). 'Consumers CAN produce X' with zero instances of X after the component's full lifetime is a hypothesis, not a finding. The one genuine, non-hypothetical gap in this space (no list semantics on the container) is confirmed separately as C-3.

killed.claim: "If this pattern is common, it belongs in the application UI layer or glass-ui as a compound primitive—not as an untyped leaf in one feature directory." + "Target a typed compound API with `as`, semantic role, density, state, leading/content/actions/detail slots, and one shared skeleton frame." (challenge-L-library.md:13,15)
killed.refutation: The conditional fails, so the conclusion never fires: the pattern is NOT common (one importer, two call sites, not exported from index.ts). Promoting a 24-line private layout div to glass-ui as a compound primitive with `as`/role/density/state axes would multiply a zero-JS shell into a producer-versioned API with no second consumer to justify it — the textbook case of feedback_kiss_no_contrivance ('don't create shared dirs or wrapper components that don't exist yet'), and it would land a demo-specific admin row grammar in the shared design system. The `detail` slot in the target API is additionally killed by C-4. Only the 'untyped' word survives, as L-1 (add defineSlots in place — no promotion, no new axes).

missed.claim: Dead required prop: `cssColorOpaque` is declared REQUIRED on AdminListItem's only consumer and is never read, forcing dead plumbing through the parent.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue:140 declares `cssColorOpaque: string;` inside defineProps<{…}> as a non-optional member. `grep -rn cssColorOpaque demo/palettes/browser/admin/` returns exactly ONE hit — that declaration. It appears nowhere in the template (:1-120) and nowhere in the script body (:122-152); it is not destructured at :132 either, so it is unreachable by any path. Because it is required, the parent is compelled to supply it: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/admin/AdminPane.vue:53 passes `:css-color-opaque="cssColorOpaque"`, sourced from `inject(CSS_COLOR_KEY)!` at AdminPane.vue:95 — a live injection wired into a black hole. Contrast the sibling AdminUsersPanel, whose analogous `:css-color` IS consumed (AdminUsersPanel.vue:145 passes it to PaletteCard), which is likely where this was copy-pasted from. Cure: delete AdminNamesPanel.vue:140 and AdminPane.vue:53. All three axes read this file (it is AdminListItem's sole consumer and the source of every slot example they cite) and none saw it.

missed.claim: The duplicated row frame has already DIVERGED: the third, uncited copy in AdminAuditPanel carries hover/transition that the primitive and the skeleton lack, so three renderings of 'the same' admin row now disagree.
missed.proof: Three verbatim copies of `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge`: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:11 (+ `min-w-0`), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListSkeleton.vue:9 (+ `skeleton-ink-register`), /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 (+ `transition-colors duration-fast hover:bg-accent/50`). challenge-L-library.md:11 names only the skeleton; no axis names AdminAuditPanel. The divergence is user-visible: an audit row lights on hover, a names row (same shell, same padding, same border) does not, and the loading skeleton matches neither state. It also proves the copies are drifting rather than merely repeating — the exact failure the 'share it structurally' cure exists to stop. Two further partial copies of the geometry prefix: AdminUsersPanel.vue:80, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:50.

missed.claim: Phantom affordance in the uncited third copy: AdminAuditPanel's row paints a hover highlight on a div with no click, keydown, role, or tabindex.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:59-63 is `<div v-for="entry in audit.entries.value" :key="entry.id" class="… transition-colors duration-fast hover:bg-accent/50">` — the element has no @click, no @keydown, no :role, no :tabindex, and nothing inside the row is interactive (:64-79 is a Badge, a timestamp span, and a target span). The background change on hover therefore promises an interaction that does not exist, and it is unreachable by keyboard or touch, so pointer users get a false signal and everyone else gets nothing. The same directory already models the correct discipline: AdminUsersPanel.vue:78-90 binds `cursor-pointer hover:bg-accent/50 focus-visible:…` AND role=button + tabindex=0 + aria-expanded + Enter/Space only when `user.paletteCount` is truthy, dropping all of it on inert rows. This is also the concrete refutation of challenge-D-design.md:14, which asks for exactly this treatment to be added to AdminListItem.

missed.claim: Sizing is specified twice and enforced zero times: the wrapper's fixed 8×8 box is re-declared by every caller (on the component's own instruction) while the wrapper does not clip a non-conforming swatch.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:13 already pins the zone at `shrink-0 w-8 h-8 flex items-center justify-center`, yet AdminListItem.vue:3 instructs callers 'Swatch slot: sized as a 8×8 leading visual (w-8 h-8 expected)', and the sole consumer duly repeats it at AdminNamesPanel.vue:46 and :96 (`class="w-8 h-8 rounded-full border border-card-edge"`). The caller could pass `w-full h-full` and be correct by construction. Worse, the duplication is unenforced in the failure direction: AdminListItem.vue:13 has NO `overflow-hidden`, so a caller who ignores the comment and slots a 48px element overflows the 32px box silently and breaks the row rhythm — the wrapper centers but never constrains. Note challenge-L-library.md:10 gets this exactly backwards, asserting the component does not supply the primitive when line 13 does.

missed.claim: Zero test coverage for the component and its only consumer.
missed.proof: `grep -rn "AdminListItem\|AdminNamesPanel" test/ e2e/` returns nothing across the repo, so neither the row shell nor the moderation queue that renders it is exercised by vitest or Playwright. This matters more than usual here because the file's raison d'être is a regression cure: AdminListItem.vue:6-10 records that the missing `min-w-0` made the moderation flow INOPERABLE at 390px (approve/reject ~250px off-card, per AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-9), and nothing in the suite would catch its removal. A single narrow-viewport assertion on the row would pin the one invariant the file exists to hold. No axis raises coverage.

superlatives: REGRESSION ARMOR, EXCELLENT — AdminListItem.vue:6-10 is a five-line comment that names the mechanism (`min-width:auto` on a grid item resolving to the flex row's min-content), the symptom (~850px track at 390px), and the cure, sitting directly above the one class it justifies (`min-w-0` at :11). The chain is complete and live: grid container with min-w-0 (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43,93) → row min-w-0 (:11) → column `flex-1 min-w-0` (:17) → `truncate` leaves (AdminNamesPanel.vue:50,52). This is the canonical CSS truncating-row recipe implemented correctly end to end, and it repaired a P0 (moderation INOPERABLE at 390px, AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-9). All three axes rendered SOURCE-RED without crediting a single line of it.

RIGHT-SIZED — the component is 13 lines of markup with zero imports, zero props, zero reactivity, zero lifecycle: no leak surface, no runtime cost, nothing to test beyond layout. For a pure three-zone shell with one consumer this is the correct size; the L-axis target API (`as` + role + density + state + four slots, challenge-L-library.md:15) would multiply it by an order of magnitude to serve two call sites.

CONSUMER A11Y, GENUINELY GOOD — every icon-only control in the slotted actions carries an item-scoped accessible name and every glyph is hidden: AdminNamesPanel.vue:55 `Approve color name ${item.name}`, :65 `Reject color name ${item.name}`, :110 `Delete color name ${item.name}`, each with `aria-hidden="true"` on the lucide icon (:56, :68, :113). challenge-L-library.md:12 speculates that delegation lets consumers 'produce … inaccessible rows'; the only consumer that exists did the opposite.

LOADING STATE IS ANNOUNCED — the paired skeleton is not a silent shape: AdminListSkeleton.vue:10-11 carries `role="status"` + `aria-label="Loading"` and mirrors the row anatomy zone-for-zone (:13 swatch, :14-17 two-line content, :18 action lozenge), so screen readers get the wait and sighted users get shape-stable loading instead of a centered spinner. Corroborated independently by the motion sweep (motion-quarantine.md:103, M-12: 'the corpus's one correct reduced-motion row'). No AdminListItem axis mentions it.

DESTRUCTIVE RESTRAINT (F-8) — the reject/delete controls rest as muted ink and turn red only on hover/focus (AdminNamesPanel.vue:64 and :109: `text-muted-foreground hover:text-destructive focus-visible:text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10`), with the rationale recorded at :58-60 ('never as a resting beacon on every row'). Applied consistently across the whole cluster (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:96, AdminUsersPanel.vue:125). challenge-D-design.md:14 lists 'destructive' among the states with 'no row-level design' — it has a deliberate, documented, cluster-wide one.

DISCIPLINED PUBLIC SURFACE — demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-8 re-exports the five panels by name and deliberately withholds AdminListItem, AdminListSkeleton, and PaginationBar, so the leaves stay private to the directory and the cluster's contract is exactly what AdminPane.vue:81-87 consumes. The L axis reads this same boundary as the defect ('an untyped leaf in one feature directory', challenge-L-library.md:13) when it is the reason the blast radius of any change here is one file.
unproven: PROVENANCE CAVEAT (governs everything above): all three AdminListItem challenge files are REPORT-AUTHORED with 0 payloads (HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:258-260, source harvest `closure-manifest-2026-08-03`). Per the ledger header (:5-8) these are 'Source-review findings — NOT challenge coverage'; no challenge seat ever ran on this component. No r2 file exists for any axis, so no AXIS-PROMOTIONS override applies and the r1 prose is the whole corpus. This is consistent with what the re-read found: 10 of 15 findings die on contact with the tree.

MOTION AXIS: vacuously clear, nothing owed. motion-quarantine.md:273 lists AdminListItem C·D·L under §7.4 'No motion content'. The only keyword hits are excluded at :299 (`challenge-L-library.md:11,15` — 'row frame'/'skeleton frame' = structural frames, not animation frames). No M-xx FALSE row touches this component, and none is carried here.

challenge-D-design.md:19 and challenge-C-implementation.md:15 prescribe RTL, 200%-text, narrow-viewport, and desktop/phone Safari audits. These are test plans, not findings — they assert no defect and I ran no browser (probe parsimony). Statically nothing in AdminListItem.vue:11-22 is direction-sensitive (no ml-/mr-/left/right; gap + flex are logical), so RTL is likely clean, but confirming it is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Whether the empty-slot gaps (C-1) or the overflow-hidden focus clip (C-5) ever render is decidable only by a consumer that triggers them; none exists today, so both are UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE in the forward direction and are filed at INFO on the strength of the source alone.

challenge-D-design.md:7's verdict phrase 'density … absent' is left unadjudicated: 'density' names no measurable property of AdminListItem.vue:11 (a single fixed px-3 py-2.5 rung with no size axis), and no consumer requests a second rung. Neither confirmed nor killed — the claim has no truth conditions.

confirmed.claim: C:12 "no prop for row variant or action absence; false geometry is unavoidable for some consumers"; D:12 "anatomy is fixed to swatch, two text lines, and action pill. Admin rows that differ will incur layout shift or promise controls they do not have"; L:12 "no variant prop represents row anatomy, density, or count".
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the corpus never supplied a single instance — all three assert it abstractly. Live: AdminListSkeleton.vue:13 renders a `w-8 h-8 rounded-full shrink-0` swatch and :18 an `h-7 w-14 rounded-full shrink-0` action pill; the `<script setup>` at :22-24 declares ZERO props (only `import { Skeleton }`), so nothing is configurable. Two consumers get shapes that do not exist: (a) AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38 renders 3 skeletons, but the real audit row at AdminAuditPanel.vue:59-63 is `class="flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge transition-colors ..."` (:62) wrapping ONLY `<div class="flex flex-col gap-0.5 min-w-0 flex-1">` (:64) — no leading swatch, no trailing action anywhere in the row (:59-79). The skeleton reserves 2rem + 0.75rem + 3.5rem + 0.75rem = 7rem of horizontal chrome that never materialises. (b) AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 renders 2 skeletons, but the real row header at :50 holds a `flex -space-x-1 shrink-0` stack (:52) of up to five `h-5 w-5` swatches (:56) ≈ 84px against the skeleton's single 32px circle, and a `font-display font-medium text-subheading truncate` title (:65) against the skeleton's `h-3.5` bar. Only AdminNamesPanel is close to faithful, and even there the real row carries TWO `h-7 px-2` buttons (AdminNamesPanel.vue:55, :62) against the skeleton's single `w-14` pill.

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:11 — "The row is coupled to `AdminListItem` only by comments and copied classes. No shared row-frame primitive guarantees that their layouts remain identical."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and understated. The frame string `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge` is independently duplicated THREE times, not two: AdminListItem.vue:11 (+`min-w-0`), AdminListSkeleton.vue:9 (bare), AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 (+`transition-colors duration-fast hover:bg-accent/50`). Only AdminNamesPanel actually consumes `<AdminListItem>` (:44, :94) — AdminAuditPanel, AdminFlaggedPanel and AdminUsersPanel hand-roll the frame. killed.claim: "Repeating several rows can create duplicate announcements" / "Multiple instances each expose role=status aria-label=Loading" — filed as an over-announcement defect.
killed.refutation: The structural redundancy is real (confirmed separately), but the claimed HARM is not demonstrable and is very likely inverted. glass-ui 7.0.0's Skeleton renders `"aria-hidden": "true"` unconditionally on every leaf and *strips* any `role`/`aria-*` fallthrough before merging (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/data-table-BygKg6ZA.js:141` `…filter(([e]) => e !== "role" && !e.startsWith("aria-"))`, `:145` `"aria-hidden": "true"`). Every child of `AdminListSkeleton.vue:10`'s `role="status"` region is therefore hidden, the region has zero text content, and a live region with no content has no delta to announce. What the corpus filed as "too many announcements" is, structurally, "no announcement at all" — see the missed finding. The exact AT behaviour on insertion of an empty populated-at-mount live region is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE; the emptiness is proven.

killed.claim: "The row is coupled to `AdminListItem` only by comments and **copied classes**."
killed.refutation: Factually wrong, and wrong in the direction that matters: they are not copies. `AdminListItem.vue:11` = `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge **min-w-0**`; `AdminListSkeleton.vue:9` = the same string with `min-w-0` MISSING. Content columns also differ: `AdminListItem.vue:17` `gap-0.5` vs `AdminListSkeleton.vue:14` `gap-1.5`. The axis asserted a state of frozen duplication as the risk; the live tree shows the drift already occurred and went unremarked — a strictly stronger finding, re-filed under missed.

killed.claim: "Vue fallthrough permits a parent to add `aria-hidden=true` to this single root, but the component has no explicit typed/owned policy coordinating that choice …"
killed.refutation: A hypothetical with no live instance and no stated cure. Zero of the five call sites pass any attr to `<AdminListSkeleton>` (`AdminAuditPanel.vue:37`, `AdminNamesPanel.vue:27`/`:77`, `AdminUsersPanel.vue:47`/`:136`, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:17` — every one is `v-for` + `:key` only). The root already hard-codes `role`+`aria-label` (`:10-11`), so a caller adding `aria-hidden` would be committing a caller error, not exercising a component defect. Ironically the named cure is one line and the producer already uses it (`inheritAttrs: !1` + attr-strip, `data-table-BygKg6ZA.js:132`/`:141`) — but that makes this an INFO-grade suggestion, not evidence for a SOURCE-RED verdict.

killed.claim: "Target: a shared `AdminListRowFrame` … with collection-level `ResourceState` owning busy/error semantics and producer motion tokens owning reduced-motion behavior."
killed.refutation: Not truth-apt against bytes; motion-quarantine row **M-15** rules the motion clause UNPROVEN and notes its premise is already satisfied — the producer owns reduced-motion via the `no-preference` gate, so that third of the target describes the shipped state rather than a change. The `ResourceState` clause is likewise pre-empted in part: error semantics are ALREADY collection-owned at all five call sites (see the D-4 kill). Only the `AdminListRowFrame` clause survives as a genuine open prescription.

missed.claim: The `.skeleton-ink-register` token seam this component's root depends on is DEAD against glass-ui 7.0.0 — the whole certified ink recipe is inert, and utils.css still documents it as live.
missed.proof: `AdminListSkeleton.vue:9` applies `skeleton-ink-register`. `demo/styles/utils.css:56-60` defines that class as exactly three custom properties: `--skeleton-ink`, `--skeleton-glass-bg`, `--skeleton-shimmer-tint`. The installed producer reads NONE of them: `grep -rn 'skeleton-glass-bg|skeleton-shimmer-tint|skeleton-shimmer-delay' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns **0 hits across the entire dist**. The served rule is `.skeleton[data-v-cd03d0b0]{ isolation:isolate; border-radius:var(--radius-input); **background:var(--muted)**; … }` (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` char 23444, reached via `demo/styles/foundation.css:57` `@import "@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles.css"` → package.json exports `./styles.css -> ./dist/glass-ui.css`), and the sheen is a hardcoded `color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 10%, transparent)`. Consequence: `demo/styles/utils.css:36-41` still asserts the ink reaches every skeleton "through glass-ui's `--skeleton-glass-bg` seam", and `:44-55` still carries the E1-R2 certification ("a CERTIFIED tone-step OF the well ground itself … guaranteed a bounded ΔL from the well in BOTH schemes by construction") — that guarantee does not reach this component, nor `AdminTagsPanel.vue:53`, nor `PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:110-111`, all of which set the same dead variable. Only `ShadowPalette.vue:104-113` still works, because it consumes `--skeleton-ink` directly. This is the exact class of regression a producer major bump causes, and the L axis — the library-boundary seat, which explicitly reasoned about producer seams at `challenge-L-library.md:9` — flagged the two inert *props* and missed the inert *token contract*. The visual consequence (whether `var(--muted)` still reads as shadow-not-content on the admin ground in both schemes) is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE; the dead seam is proven.

missed.claim: The collection-level `aria-label` that all five call sites rely on is silently dropped by every conforming engine — the wrapper is a bare `<div>` with no `role`, and ARIA `generic` prohibits naming.
missed.proof: Every AdminListSkeleton wrapper is `<div class="grid gap-…" aria-label="Loading …">` with no `role`: `AdminAuditPanel.vue:36` ("Loading audit log"), `AdminUsersPanel.vue:46` ("Loading users") and `:135` ("Loading palettes"), `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16` ("Loading flagged palettes"), `AdminNamesPanel.vue:26` ("Loading pending proposals") and `:76` ("Loading approved names"). A `<div>` with no role maps to ARIA `generic`, and `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` are in `generic`'s *Prohibited States and Properties* — the name is discarded, not merely ignored. So six author-written, context-specific loading names reach no user, while 2-3 unlabelled-in-practice `role="status"` shells sit inside each. This is precisely the boundary all three axes prescribed moving status semantics *to* (`challenge-D-design.md:19`, `challenge-L-library.md:11`, `challenge-C-implementation.md:9`) — none noticed the container already attempts it and fails silently. The in-house counter-example, one file over, is `AdminTagsPanel.vue:52-55`, which adds `role="status"` to the wrapper and therefore *does* get its name: the fix is one attribute at six sites.

missed.claim: Net effect at runtime: the admin loading state is announced to nobody. The corpus filed the opposite defect.
missed.proof: Synthesis of two proven facts. (1) The container's name is discarded (see the `generic` finding above). (2) Every leaf inside the `role="status"` region is force-hidden by the producer: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/data-table-BygKg6ZA.js:145` emits `"aria-hidden": "true"` unconditionally and `:141` strips `role`/`aria-*` out of fallthrough, so `AdminListSkeleton.vue:13,15,16,18` contribute zero accessible content. A live region whose entire content is `aria-hidden` has no delta to announce; `AdminListSkeleton.vue:11`'s static `aria-label="Loading"` is a *name*, discoverable only by deliberate navigation, and does not fire an announcement. Combined with the confirmed absence of any completion signal (C-5 / M-09) and the absence of `aria-busy` anywhere in `demo/palettes/browser/admin/`, a screen-reader user experiences silence during load followed by rows that appear without comment. Both `challenge-D-design.md:11` and `challenge-C-implementation.md:9` diagnosed over-announcement; the live tree shows under-announcement. Exact AT behaviour on live-region insertion is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE; the zero-announceable-content structure is proven.

missed.claim: The skeleton has already drifted from the `AdminListItem` row frame it exists to mirror, dropping a documented invariant and a spacing value.
missed.proof: `demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue:11` carries `min-w-0` on the row root, with a five-line comment immediately above it (`:6-10`) naming the invariant and the bug it fixed: "S.W5-12 (F-1): min-w-0 on the ROW ITSELF — the row is a grid item, and its min-width:auto automatic minimum resolves to the flex row's min-content (the un-breakable nowrap spans), blowing the track to ~850px at 390." `AdminListSkeleton.vue:9` — a grid item in exactly the same structural position, inside the same `grid gap-…` containers — omits it. The content column also diverges: `AdminListItem.vue:17` `gap-0.5` (0.125rem) vs `AdminListSkeleton.vue:14` `gap-1.5` (0.375rem). Honest bound: the `min-w-0` omission is currently harmless because every skeleton child is `shrink-0` or already `min-w-0`, so its min-content is ~8.5rem — well under a 390px track. The defect is that an invariant documented as load-bearing is unenforced on the one file written to be geometrically identical, and the 0.25rem gap delta is a live shadow-vs-real mismatch. This is the concrete drift `challenge-L-library.md:10` predicted while misdescribing the classes as copies.

missed.claim: AdminAuditPanel's loading grid rhythm does not match its loaded rhythm, compounding the swap shift.
missed.proof: `AdminAuditPanel.vue:36` renders the three skeletons inside `class="grid gap-2"`, but the real entries are direct children of the panel root `class="grid gap-3 pb-3"` (`:2`, v-for at `:59`). So row spacing tightens to 0.5rem during load and loosens to 0.75rem after — on top of the ~2.75rem horizontal inset shift already confirmed for this panel. The other panels are internally consistent (`AdminUsersPanel.vue:46` gap-3 / `:64` gap-3; `AdminNamesPanel.vue:26` gap-2 / `:43` gap-2), which isolates the audit panel as the outlier rather than a systemic choice. No axis inspected the wrapper's spacing.

missed.claim: `data-slot="admin-list-skeleton"` is unconsumed metadata.
missed.proof: `AdminListSkeleton.vue:8` declares it, and `grep -rn 'admin-list-skeleton' demo/` returns exactly that one line — no CSS selector, no test, no query. The convention itself is house-legitimate (5 sites in `demo/`) and one sibling actually uses it as a styling hook (`PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:33` declared, `:120` selected as `[data-slot="palette-card-skeleton"]`), so this is consistency, not waste — recorded only so the next reader does not assume a hook exists.

superlatives: ONE loading grammar, propagated with provenance. `AdminListSkeleton.vue:2-6` names the wave, the invariant, the sibling it matches, and what it replaced — "Replaces the generic centered `Loader2` spinner in every admin panel" — and the call sites carry the same intent forward in their own voice: `AdminUsersPanel.vue:44-45` ("never a centered generic spinner"), `AdminAuditPanel.vue:35`, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:15`, `AdminTagsPanel.vue:49-50`. An entire admin surface converted from spinner to row-shadow, with the reasoning legible at every site. This is unusually good.

Proportional text bars. `AdminListSkeleton.vue:15-16` pair fixed widths with `max-w-[60%]` / `max-w-[40%]` inside a `flex-1 min-w-0` column (`:14`), with both fixed neighbours `shrink-0` (`:13`, `:18`). The shadow's text rhythm degrades proportionally in narrow containers — the exact property `challenge-C-implementation.md:10` and `challenge-D-design.md:15` claimed was absent.

Text-size resilience by construction. Every utility here is rem-derived (Tailwind v4's `--spacing` base is un-overridden across `demo/styles/` and `glass-ui/dist/styles/`), so the whole shadow scales 1:1 with a user's root font-size preference. The 200%-text audit cell demanded at `challenge-D-design.md:19` is already satisfied without a line of media query.

Motion correctly delegated. The component authors zero motion and inherits the producer's scan, which is the ONLY `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` gate in all of `glass-ui.css` (motion-quarantine M-12) — declaration absent under `reduce`, not clamped (`glass-ui.css` char 23781; M-10 measurement). Centrally governed motion is the right architecture, and this file is a clean instance of it.

error ≠ empty, at every single call site. `AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53`, `AdminUsersPanel.vue:51-62`, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-32`, `AdminNamesPanel.vue:30-41` and `:80-91` each interpose `<EmptyState variant="error">` + Retry between loading and empty, with `loading` cleared in a `finally` (`useAdminAudit.ts:68-69`). A dead backend can never costume as a clear ledger — the panels' own comments name this "the P0 case". `challenge-D-design.md:14` asserted the opposite.

The cure for the status-boundary defect is already written, in the same directory. `AdminTagsPanel.vue:52-63` is the container-owned pattern in full: one `role="status" aria-label="Loading tags"` on the wrapper, N bare `<Skeleton>` children, alternating widths for rhythm. Any remediation of AdminListSkeleton should copy this file, not invent a `ResourceState` abstraction.
unproven: Whether the served `var(--muted)` skeleton block (glass-ui's default, since `--skeleton-glass-bg` is dead — see missed #1) still reads as SHADOW rather than content against the admin panel ground in BOTH schemes. The E1-R2 ΔL certification at `demo/styles/utils.css:44-55` no longer applies to this component; re-certification needs live measurement. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Exact assistive-technology behaviour on insertion of a `role="status"` region whose entire content is `aria-hidden` (missed #3, and the kill of D-1/C-1). Screen readers differ on announcing live regions added to the DOM; the zero-announceable-content structure is proven statically, the resulting silence is not. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Whether the confirmed geometry mismatch (D-2/C-4/L-4) produces a measurable CLS at AdminUsersPanel (~0.75rem × 3 rows) and AdminAuditPanel (~2.75rem horizontal inset). The structural mismatch is proven from source; the layout-shift magnitude is not. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

The `AdminListRowFrame` prescription (`challenge-L-library.md:14`, `challenge-D-design.md:19`) — prescriptive, not truth-apt against bytes. Its motion clause is pre-empted (motion-quarantine M-15) and its error-semantics clause is pre-empted (see the D-4 kill); only the shared-frame clause is a live open question.

Whether a slow-but-not-failing request can strand the skeleton in practice — there is no AbortController or timeout anywhere in `demo/palettes/api/`, so the `finally` at `useAdminAudit.ts:68-69` never runs for a hung fetch. Requires a network-throttled live probe to decide whether this is reachable. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:15 — 'The row has a border/radius but no signature connection to the admin information architecture; it risks becoming a generic card repeated everywhere.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and materially understated — not a taste risk, a named canon defect. AdminListItem.vue:11 ships `rounded-md border border-card-edge`, a FOUR-sided stroke per row. docs/tranches/V/OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md:83 grants Admin·Names exactly 'one low-emphasis separator between adjacent review rows; none after the final row'; :90 states 'Any additional line, automatic P122 divider, consumer-hidden producer line, terminal row rule, caster stroke or corner rule is a defect.' The last row's bottom border IS the named terminal row rule. Compounding: the field already separates by interval (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43 `grid gap-2`) and adds a fifth stroke per row on the swatch (AdminNamesPanel.vue:46 `border border-card-edge`) — one boundary expressed three times, the exact case docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:69 law 4 forbids ('Spacing plus material already expressing the same boundary makes the line duplicative'). Cure is one class edit at AdminListItem.vue:11.

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:11 — 'The row frame is duplicated in AdminListSkeleton instead of shared structurally.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and undercounted by 3x. The literal class string `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5` appears in FIVE independent places, none importing another: AdminListItem.vue:11, AdminListSkeleton.vue:9, AdminUsersPanel.vue:80, AdminAuditPanel.vue:62, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:50. The content-column grammar `flex flex-col gap-0.5 min-w-0 flex-1` is re-typed at AdminAuditPanel.vue:64 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:61 versus AdminListItem.vue:17. Only AdminNamesPanel.vue:128 imports AdminListItem. docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 binds 'Admin is a five-route review suite—Users, Names, Audit, Flagged and Tags—using one review-row anatomy'; the anatomy exists as five copies, so 1 of 5 routes consumes the component that names it.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:12 — 'There is no detail/disclosure region even though admin rows often need it; consumers may create detached siblings.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — the predicted consequence is already realised in the live tree, which the axis did not know. AdminUsersPanel.vue:68 wraps its row in `rounded-md border border-card-edge overflow-hidden` and hangs the disclosure body as a detached sibling at :134 (`border-t border-border bg-muted/30 px-3 py-3`), re-typing the row grammar at :80 rather than importing AdminListItem. AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:47 + :50 use the identical detached-sibling shape. So 'consumers may create detached siblings' is not speculation: two of the five Admin routes did exactly that, and the cost is the border-duplication defect confirmed under D-5.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 — 'The root has no role, item ID, selected state, disabled state, or keyboard contract.'
confirmed.proof: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — only the role limb survives. AdminListItem.vue:11 is a bare `<div>` with no role/tabindex/handler, and the field wrapper (AdminNamesPanel.vue:43, :93) is `grid gap-2` — a grep for `role=`, `<ul`, `<li`, `<ol` across demo/palettes/browser/admin/*.vue returns zero list semantics anywhere in the suite, so AT announces N unrelated groups instead of a list of N proposals. The remaining limbs are refuted: `ProposedColorName` (demo/color-session/color-names.ts:12-20) carries no selected/disabled/expanded field, the tab strip already partitions on `status`, and the row is deliberately non-interactive so it owes no keyboard contract — its two commands carry their own accessible names (AdminNamesPanel.vue:55, :65). Note the canon's nearest text (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:186) forbids listbox/option fiction, not role=list, so the residual cure is `role="list"`/`listitem`, never a listbox.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:14 — 'Hover, focus-within, selected, disabled, destructive, pending, and expanded states have no row-level design.'
confirmed.proof: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED, on the hover/focus-within limb only, and the real defect is divergence rather than absence. AdminListItem.vue:11 carries no hover, focus-within or transition. Its sibling review rows DO: AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 `transition-colors duration-fast hover:bg-accent/50`, AdminUsersPanel.vue:80-83 `transition-colors` + `hover:bg-accent/50 focus-visible:bg-accent/50 focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`. Three routes, three different row-level state designs, against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:218 'one review-row anatomy'. Refuted limbs: selected/disabled/expanded/pending are not states of this row — no such field exists on `ProposedColorName` (demo/color-session/color-names.ts:12-20) and the row is non-interactive by design; 'destructive' is carried by the button, not the row (AdminNamesPanel.vue:64).

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:12 — 'Action semantics, item semantics, selection, disclosure, and navigation are all delegated, so consumers can produce incompatible or inaccessible rows under the same visual shell.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED on the fact (AdminListItem.vue has no <script> block at all — the whole file is 24 lines of template, so every semantic is delegated) and on the consequence, though the consequence lands across the COPIES rather than across this component's own two call sites (which are identical, AdminNamesPanel.vue:44-71 and :94-116). Realised divergence under the same visual shell: AdminUsersPanel.vue:85-88 makes the row a real `role=button` + tabindex + aria-expanded disclosure; AdminAuditPanel.vue:62 makes it hover-lit but inert; AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:50 makes it fully inert with no hover; AdminListItem.vue:11 makes it inert with no hover. Four semantics, one visual shell.

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:9 — 'There are no imports, props, or types: reuse occurs through three unconstrained slots and copied class expectations.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED verbatim. demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminListItem.vue is 24 lines, `<template>` only — no `<script setup>`, no `defineProps`, no `defineSlots`, no imports (compare AdminListSkeleton.vue:22-24, which does have a script block). The only constraint on slot content is the prose at :2-5. Reported as INFO, not a defect on its own: with one importer (AdminNamesPanel.vue:128) and two identical call sites, an untyped slot leaf is the KISS-correct shape; the defect is what the prose says (see MISSED), not that props are absent.

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:10 — 'Comments specify an expected 8×8 swatch and typography, but the component neither supplies nor validates those primitives.'
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED on the fact, but the axis picked the weaker half. AdminListItem.vue:13 DOES supply the 8×8 box (`shrink-0 w-8 h-8 flex items-center justify-center`) — so that limb is half-wrong; the consumer then re-declares `w-8 h-8` inside it (AdminNamesPanel.vue:46, :96), redundant but harmless. The typography limb is confirmed and worse than 'unvalidated': the prescription at :4-5 is factually contradicted by every shipped implementation (see MISSED — the comment says `text-caption`, the live rows ship `text-mono-small`).

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:13 — 'Truncation is delegated to content supplied by callers; the wrapper only hides overflow, potentially clipping focus rings or important text.'
killed.refutation: KILLED on its distinctive assertion. `overflow-hidden` exists in exactly one place, the CONTENT column (AdminListItem.vue:17). The root (:11 `flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge min-w-0`) has no overflow clip, and the actions cluster (:20 `flex items-center gap-1.5 shrink-0`) is a separate flex item outside the clipped box — so every button focus ring escapes freely. No focusable element is ever placed in the content slot: both call sites supply two plain non-focusable `<span>`s (AdminNamesPanel.vue:50/52 and :100/102). There is therefore no focus ring to clip, in the live tree or in the component's contract. The residual true half — clipped IMPORTANT TEXT — is real but has a different mechanism than the axis names (it is `truncate` on the spans, not `overflow-hidden` on the wrapper) and no accessible fallback; re-filed under MISSED with the correct mechanism and provenance.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:10 — 'Arbitrary slot content can violate expected dimensions, overflow, or contain nested interactive controls with conflicting row behavior.'
killed.refutation: KILLED — the hazard requires a row behavior that does not exist. AdminListItem.vue:11 has no @click, no @keydown, no tabindex, no role: there is nothing for a nested control to conflict WITH. Nested-interactive conflict is a real hazard in this suite, but it lives at AdminUsersPanel.vue:80-89, where the row IS a `role=button` with tabindex and Enter/Space handling and contains a Trash button at :126 — and that component does not use AdminListItem. The claim is misattributed. 'Arbitrary slot content' is also unrealised: two call sites, byte-identical anatomy (AdminNamesPanel.vue:45-70, :95-115).

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:13 — 'The trailing action cluster can grow without a width/overflow policy and can squeeze identity content on phone widths.'
killed.refutation: KILLED — an explicit, documented policy exists and is the component's whole reason for being. AdminListItem.vue:20 puts `shrink-0` on the actions cluster, :17 puts `flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-hidden` on the content column, and :11 puts `min-w-0` on the row itself; :6-10 states the policy in full, naming the grid-item `min-width:auto` mechanism it cures. The direction of squeeze is therefore DELIBERATE and inverted from the claim: identity truncates so the commands stay on-card. AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-9 records the pre-cure state — approve/reject pushed ~250px off-card, the moderation flow INOPERABLE at 390px. Live worst case is two `h-7 px-2` buttons with 14px glyphs (AdminNamesPanel.vue:55, :61), ~66px total. What is missing is not a width policy but an accessible fallback for the truncated text — filed under MISSED.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:12 — 'Swatch, content, and actions are visual slots with no labels or required anatomy. Empty slots still reserve space.'
killed.refutation: KILLED as over-general. Only ONE of the three slots reserves space: the swatch wrapper is hard-sized `w-8 h-8` (AdminListItem.vue:13). The content column is `flex-1` (:17) — it reserves nothing of its own, it absorbs. The actions cluster (:20) has no width declaration at all, so an empty actions slot collapses to 0px. The accurate residue is narrower than stated and is already carried by C-1: an empty swatch leaves 32px + a 12px `gap-3`, and an empty actions slot still leaves a 12px `gap-3` (so a 24px right inset against a 12px `px-3` left inset). Both are inert: zero call sites omit either slot.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:5 — 'SOURCE-RED. The implementation cannot enforce the semantic or layout invariants its comments promise.'
killed.refutation: KILLED on the LAYOUT half, which is the half the component actually promises. The layout invariant stated at AdminListItem.vue:6-10 is enforced completely and structurally by the very next lines: `min-w-0` on the row (:11), `flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-hidden` on the content column (:17), `shrink-0` on both flanks (:13, :20). No consumer can defeat it from inside a slot — a slot child cannot raise its ancestor's min-width. The SEMANTIC half of the verdict stands (see C-3 confirmed), but the verdict as written indicts the one invariant this file provably delivers.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:5 — 'This is a reusable primitive in practice but has no explicit library contract.'
killed.refutation: KILLED — the premise 'reusable primitive in practice' is false in the live tree. AdminListItem has exactly ONE importer (AdminNamesPanel.vue:128) and two call sites (:44, :94), both inside that same file. It is deliberately absent from the cluster's public surface: demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts exports five panels ('NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)') and does not export AdminListItem, AdminListSkeleton or PaginationBar. The library-boundary framing therefore inverts the actual defect, which is not unconstrained reuse but non-adoption: the row anatomy this file names is hand-copied by the four sibling routes instead (see L-11 confirmed).

missed.claim: The component's only contract prose is factually WRONG about the shipped typography, and it instructs future consumers to violate a later ruling. AdminListItem.vue:4-5 prescribes the secondary line as 'text-caption text-muted-foreground'. `text-caption` is ITALIC by definition (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/semantic.css: `@utility text-caption { font-family: var(--font-text); font-size: var(--type-caption); line-height: var(--type-leading-caption); font-style: italic; }`). Every shipped implementation refuses it: AdminNamesPanel.vue:52 and :102 use `text-mono-small`, and AdminNamesPanel.vue:11-12 states the reason — 'F-9: the secondary line is a CSS literal — a READOUT: Fira, never italic display type'. AdminAuditPanel.vue:74-78 repeats the same ruling verbatim for its own secondary line. Three implementations, zero honour the comment; the comment was never updated. confirmed.id: L-r2 L-3 — the imperative registry retains unmounted cards; verdicts are silently lost

Vue invokes a function ref with `null` on unmount; the `el &&` short-circuit swallows that call, so `cardRefs` (declared `reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({})` at BrowsePane.vue:209 / PalettesPane.vue:177) never deletes. Three independent producers pass `""` straight through, because each falls back only on nullish or non-Error, never on empty string: useBrowsePalettes.ts:152 `e?.message ?? killed.id: D#4 first limb — "The compact absolute/inline placement contract is unstated… can overlap card content" (challenge-D-design.md:14)

killed.id: C#5 — "the parent cannot distinguish automatic expiry from user acknowledgement" (challenge-C-implementation.md:13)

ActionFeedback.vue:1-17 has no `@click`, no close control, no `tabindex`, no focusable descendant; :33-35 declares exactly one emit; :44 is its only call site, inside the setTimeout. The genuine gap is the total absence of a dismiss affordance — which D's target gestalt already prescribes at challenge-D-design.md:19 ("error persists with keyboard-focusable Retry/Dismiss"). KeepAlive (demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:2) deactivates rather than unmounts, so it creates no mount-with-true either.
