killed.refutation: Duplicate of nothing. Re-verified independently of r2: `grep -rln "text-green-600|bg-green-500/10|green-400" demo src` returns exactly one file — this one; `grep -rn "bg-green-500/10" demo | wc -l` → 1. There is no second hand-rolled verdict chip in the demo. It is a SINGLETON FORK of the producer tone register (r2 C7, challenge-L-library-r2.md:75-77). The routing consequence is material: nothing needs deduplicating, one class attribute needs re-tokenising.

killed.id: L r1 #5 + target #16 — route the verdict to the producer's toast/alert contract
killed.claim: The component "hand-builds a toast/status primitive … outside the producer's alert/toast/result contracts"; the cure is a shared `ActionResult` primitive.
killed.refutation: The prescribed cure is structurally wrong. glass-ui 7.0.0 does export `./toast`, and it is a VIEWPORT-anchored global toaster — dist/components/toast/Toaster.vue.d.ts types its only prop as `ToasterPosition = "top-left" | … | "bottom-right"`. ActionFeedback is an in-card, in-flow chip that unfurls inside the card body between the rename row and the swatch drawer (PaletteCard.vue:112-158). Routing it to Toast would relocate every palette verdict to a screen corner and sever it from the card it describes — a UX regression sold as a conformance win. r2's C8 (challenge-L-library-r2.md:79-83) reaches the same conclusion. The RED grade survives; the reason given for it does not.

killed.id: L r1 #12 — "not scoped to a producer motion token or reduced-motion policy" (challenge-L-library.md:12)
killed.claim: The transition class family is globally named and is scoped to neither a producer motion token nor a reduced-motion policy.
killed.refutation: Second and third limbs REFUTED — quarantined FALSE at codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:98 (M-07), file-level disposition :260. Re-verified against bytes: demo/styles/animations.css:142-155 consumes `--duration-fast`, `--ease-decelerate`, `--spring-bouncy`, `--spring-bouncy-duration`, `--duration-normal`, `--ease-accelerate` — 6 of 6 defined in glass-ui dist/styles (scheme-motion.css, scheme-spring.css, theme/bridges.css) with zero demo re-definitions. The reduced-motion policy is not merely present but deliberate: the producer guard strips `transform` and `max-height` from the transition set entirely, surgically removing the bouncy spring and the height morph while leaving a 100 ms fade. Only the "globally named" limb is true, and it is a description of a correct central-governance architecture, not a defect.

killed.id: L-r2 L-1's prescribed CURE — "`bg-success/10 text-success`, drop the `dark:` variant" (challenge-L-library-r2.md:114), and its scoping note at :110
killed.claim: "Honest scoping: this is not a contrast regression — the forked ink is darker in light mode, so it reads slightly stronger. The defect is ownership." Route: adopt `bg-success/10 text-success`.
killed.refutation: The DEFECT stands (confirmed above) but the CURE is unsound and the scoping note is contrast-blind. Computed from token bytes with standard sRGB alpha compositing: ground = `--well-bg: color-mix(in oklab, var(--card) 92%, var(--foreground) 8%)` (demo/styles/foundation.css:328) applied at PaletteCard.vue:19 (`bg-well`) → #e9e1d9 light. Shipped success ink (green-600) on `bg-green-500/10` over that ground = 2.31:1. Swap to `text-success` (`--success` light = `oklch(0.720 0.192 149.5)`, glass-ui dist/styles/tokens/color-radius.css) and it becomes 1.65:1 — the cure drops contrast by a further 29%. The r2 compared fork-vs-token and concluded correctly that the fork is DARKER; it never compared either against the ground they both sit on. Adopting the tone token here is right on ownership and wrong on legibility, and must be shipped together with an ink rung (see missed).

killed.id: L-r2 L-6's premise — glass-ui `Chip` sm is "a near-transcription of what this file hand-rolls" (challenge-L-library-r2.md:83, 215)
killed.claim: `chipVariants` sm = `"gap-1 px-2.5 py-1 text-caption"` is the same recipe as ActionFeedback.vue:7, so adopting `Chip mode="static"` is a small, like-for-like swap.
killed.refutation: Over-stated on two axes — this is a layout AND typeface change, not a re-tokenisation. (1) TYPEFACE: glass-ui's `text-caption` is `@utility text-caption { font-family: var(--font-text); font-size: var(--type-caption); font-style: italic; }` — an ITALIC text-font. The shipped chip is `fira-code` mono (ActionFeedback.vue:7, demo/styles/utils.css:9). Adopting Chip sm flips a monospaced verdict into italic prose. (2) LAYOUT: `Chip` is a pill capsule — chipVariants declares `shape.pill`, and dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css gives `.glass-chip--icon`/`--cell` explicit `--radius-pill`/`--radius-card` rungs. The shipped element is BLOCK-LEVEL: `flex` with no `inline-flex`, no `w-fit`, no `self-start`, and no width constraint from PaletteCard.vue:123-128, so its tint spans the full card width. Swapping to Chip shrink-wraps the tint to the text. L-6's underlying observation — that Chip has one adopter repo-wide (verified: only demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14 imports it) and this is live under-adoption — survives. Its "same recipe" premise, and therefore its "small" cost estimate, does not.

missed.claim: Both tone rungs fail WCAG 1.4.3 AA at their shipped 12 px size, and the DARK error rung — the exact rung the r2 canonises as superlative S-4 — is the worst contrast in the component. No axis mentions contrast at all.
missed.proof: Derived from token bytes + standard sRGB alpha compositing (Tailwind v4's `/10` modifier emits `color-mix(in oklab, X 10%, transparent)`, i.e. alpha 0.1 over the ground). Ground: PaletteCard.vue:19 applies `bg-well`; demo/styles/foundation.css:143,328 define `--color-well: var(--well-bg)` and `--well-bg: color-mix(in oklab, var(--card) 92%, var(--foreground) 8%)`; token arms from glass-ui dist/styles/tokens/color-radius.css + dark-arm.css. Computed ratios — LIGHT ground #e9e1d9: success ink green-600 on `bg-green-500/10` = 2.31:1; destructive ink `hsl(0 72% 50%)` on `bg-destructive/10` = 3.27:1. DARK ground #42372f: success ink green-400 = 5.64:1 (the ONLY passing rung); destructive ink `hsl(0 80% 60%)` = 2.78:1. Required: 4.5:1 — ActionFeedback.vue:7 sets `text-xs` (0.75 rem = 12 px, not "large text"), so three of four rungs fail AA and two fail even the 3:1 non-text floor. This is the axis-crossing miss: the D axis owns contrast and never looked; the L axis looked at the same two lines (challenge-L-library-r2.md:100-110) and explicitly disclaimed contrast at :110; and challenge-L-library-r2.md:239-241 elevates `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` to a superlative ("byte-identical to --destructive", "the correct pattern is already in the file") on a light-mode-only measurement, while in dark mode that same pair is the component's worst reading at 2.78:1.

missed.claim: The root cause of the tone fork is a gap in the PRODUCER's sealed axis, not consumer sloppiness: the tone register ships fill + ink-on-fill and has no on-surface ink rung, so any consumer wanting a tinted status chip must invent one. This is the finding the L axis should have relayed to glass-ui instead of (or alongside) narrowing `ChipVisualProps["tone"]`.
missed.proof: glass-ui dist/styles/tokens/color-radius.css ships each tone as a PAIR: `--success: oklch(0.720 0.192 149.5)` with `--success-foreground: var(--neutral-0)` (near-white), likewise `--warning`/`--warning-foreground`, `--info`/`--info-foreground`, `--destructive`/`--destructive-foreground`. That pairing is a FILL and the ink that sits ON the fill — it is designed for a solid `bg-success` + white text, which reads fine. There is no `--success-ink` / `--on-success-subtle` rung for the tinted-surface case, and dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts seals the axis at five names with no ink dimension. ActionFeedback.vue:8 reaching for Tailwind green-600 is the predictable consequence: green-600 is the nearest available token-shaped thing that is dark enough to be read on a 10% tint. The correct routing is a producer ask (add the ink rung to the sealed cohort) plus a consumer fix that lands on it — not the local one-liner at challenge-L-library-r2.md:114, which regresses legibility. challenge-L-library-r2.md:217 already opens a BJ relay channel on `Chip`'s tone typing; this is the more load-bearing item to put on it.

missed.claim: Typography fork, one token to the LEFT of the colour fork in the same class string, and missed by all three axes: `text-xs fira-code` is a hand-rolled, NON-FLUID reconstruction of the producer's `text-mono-small` utility.
missed.proof: ActionFeedback.vue:7 `'feedback-chip flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-panel text-xs fira-code'`. `grep -rn "text-xs fira-code" demo --include="*.vue"` returns exactly ONE file — this one. Census: 28 demo `.vue` files use `text-mono-small`; only 3 use `text-xs` at all. Every sibling in the same folder is on the register: PaletteCard.vue:64,72 `text-mono-small`; PaletteCardMenu.vue:37,57 `fira-code text-mono-caption`, :101,112 `text-caption`; PaletteCardMeta.vue:53 `text-mono-small`; PaletteCardSwatches.vue:9 `text-mono-small`. The producer utility is `@utility text-mono-small { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-small); line-height: var(--type-leading-small); }` — i.e. exactly `fira-code` + a size. The consequence goes beyond ownership: `--type-small` is `clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem)` (fluid), while `text-xs` is a FIXED 0.75 rem. So the verdict text is the one string in the card that does not participate in the fluid type ramp — at a wide viewport the sibling `Badge` at PaletteCard.vue:72 grows toward 1.25 rem while the verdict stays pinned at 12 px, and the gap widens with the window. It is also the direct cause of the AA failure above (at 0.875 rem+ the 3.27:1 destructive rung would still fail, but the threshold conversation changes).

missed.claim: `--vj-celebrate-expanded: 2.5rem` is a hard-coded height for content of unbounded height; a two-line message is clipped through the entire enter transition and then pops open, and snaps down before the leave.
missed.proof: ActionFeedback.vue:54-56 sets `--vj-celebrate-collapse: 0px; --vj-celebrate-expanded: 2.5rem;`. demo/styles/animations.css:161 and :164-165 map those onto `max-height` at `-enter-from`/`-leave-to` and `-enter-to`/`-leave-from`, with `overflow: hidden` on both active classes (:147, :154). Measured from the box model: one line = `py-1.5` (6 px × 2) + a 16 px line box (`text-xs` line-height `calc(1 / 0.75)` = 1.333 × 12 px) = 28 px, comfortably inside 40 px. Two lines = 12 + 32 = 44 px > 40 px, so the chip is clipped 4 px for the whole `--duration-normal` enter and then jumps open the instant Vue removes `-enter-active`/`-enter-to` and `max-height` reverts to `none`; on leave, `-leave-from` re-imposes 40 px and snaps it DOWN before collapsing. Three lines makes it a 20 px pop. Reachable: the wall is `grid-cols-1` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4) so cards are pane-wide on desktop, but at phone width a 46-character message — e.g. usePaletteActions.ts:56 `Failed to publish: ${msg}` — wraps at 12 px mono. The scoped block is otherwise exemplary (see superlatives); this is the one number in it that assumes something it cannot know.

missed.claim: The perceptual half of L-4, which no axis states: a replacement verdict mutates in place with NO enter beat, no focus move and no announcement — the component's single "something happened" affordance is precisely the one a replacement suppresses.
missed.proof: challenge-L-library-r2.md:170-192 measures the CLOCK (VERDICT-B lives 701 ms) and stops there. The design consequence is separate and arguably worse. `<Transition name="vj-celebrate">` (ActionFeedback.vue:3) fires only on the `v-if` toggle at :5; when a second verdict arrives while the first is up, `visible` stays `true`, so no enter runs. Only `message` (:14), the tint (:8-9) and the icon (:12-13) swap. A success→error replacement therefore changes a chip from green-with-a-checkmark to red-with-an-alert with ZERO motion — and with no `aria-live` (see D#2) and no focus management, there is no channel of ANY modality signalling that a new, contradictory result landed. A user who publishes then immediately makes-private (BrowsePane.vue:249 twice) can watch "Published" become "Failed to update visibility" with no perceptual event marking the change, and then watch it vanish 701 ms later on the first verdict's clock.

missed.claim: The two lucide icons break the repo's own 71-instance `aria-hidden` convention, including six instances inside this very feature.
missed.proof: ActionFeedback.vue:12-13 render `<CheckCircle2 class="w-3.5 h-3.5 shrink-0" />` and `<AlertCircle class="w-3.5 h-3.5 shrink-0" />` with no `aria-hidden`. @lucide/vue@1.17.0 supplies none by default — dist/esm/defaultAttributes.mjs sets only `xmlns/width/height/viewBox/fill/stroke/stroke-width/stroke-linecap/stroke-linejoin`, and dist/esm/Icon.mjs adds only `class` — so each icon reaches the a11y tree as an unnamed graphic. The repo's standing convention is explicit and dense: `grep -rn 'aria-hidden="true"' demo --include="*.vue"` → 71 hits, six of them in this feature (PaletteCard.vue:103, PaletteSlugBar.vue:26,27,38,85, CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:47,50,53), and ShadowPalette.vue:37-44 and PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:30 both argue the semantics out in comments. This is cosmetic today only because nothing announces the chip at all; the moment D#2's live region lands, an unnamed graphic sits inside the announced region and the cure regresses the announcement.

missed.claim: `feedback-chip` is not a chip. It is a full-bleed band wearing a panel radius — the element's material register is unreconciled with both of the producer registers it borrows from.
missed.proof: ActionFeedback.vue:7 uses `flex` (block-level, NOT `inline-flex`) with no `w-fit`/`self-start`/`max-w-*`, and PaletteCard.vue:123-128 wraps it in nothing, so its tinted background spans the full card width — the `px-3 py-1.5` are interior padding, not an inset. Its radius is `rounded-panel` = `--radius-panel: var(--radius-xl)` = 12 px (glass-ui dist/styles/theme/radius.css) — the PANEL rung, on a 28 px-tall status element, while the producer's chip register uses `--radius-pill` (9999 px) for `pill` and `--radius-card` for `cell` (dist/styles/glass/glass-chip.css). Nor is its vertical rhythm reconciled with its neighbours: the metadata row above is `px-3 py-2.5` (PaletteCard.vue:43) and the chip is `py-1.5` with no margin, so a full-width red band butts flush against a 10 px-padded row. A full-bleed alert bar may well be the RIGHT gestalt for a card verdict — it is closer to D's "result ledger anchored to the action" (challenge-D-design.md:19) than a pill is — but the file names itself a chip, dresses as a panel, and lays out as a band, and no axis noticed the three disagree.

missed.claim: No overflow discipline on the message span, in a card that explicitly refuses to clip — the one true residue of D#4.
missed.proof: ActionFeedback.vue:14 `{{ message }}` sits directly in the `flex` row at :7 with no `min-w-0`, no `truncate`, no `break-words`, no `line-clamp`. Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, so an unbreakable long token cannot shrink below its intrinsic width. The card root then declines to contain it — PaletteCard.vue:16-18 states the rule in a comment: "NO overflow-hidden (S.W5-10 / S-15-A): a card-level radius clip rasterizes 1-bit at compositing-layer bounds". The messages that reach this span are unsanitised thrown-error text (useBrowsePalettes.ts:152, :215; useDialogBrowseActions.ts:70), which can carry a URL, a slug, or a stack fragment with no break opportunity. Every sibling that renders user or API text guards it — PaletteCardSwatches.vue:9 `truncate max-w-tooltip`, PaletteCard.vue:55 `line-clamp-2 sm:line-clamp-1`. This one does not.

missed.claim: The card owns a verdict surface and never uses it for its own two locally-handled fallible actions: both `writeClipboard` calls discard a discriminated result the producer went out of its way to provide.
missed.proof: PaletteCard.vue:294 `copyAll: () => void writeClipboard(props.palette.colors.map((c) => c.css).join(", "))` and :333 `onPopoverCopy` → `void writeClipboard(css)`. The producer's signature is `writeClipboard(text: string): Promise<CopyResult>` where `CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason }`, and glass-ui dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:33-37 documents the intent verbatim: "Returns the discriminated result (`{ ok }` / `{ ok, reason }`) rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)`." The `void` operator discards it, and `CopyFailureReason` is `"clipboard-api" | "no-api"` — i.e. exactly the Safari/permissions/insecure-context failures that are silent by nature. Meanwhile ActionFeedback is mounted 170 lines above at :123-128 and `showFeedback` is in scope at :238. This is the design-axis complement to L-3: L-3 says verdicts are lost in transit; this says two verdicts are never generated, from the only two actions the card handles itself rather than emitting upward.

missed.claim: Zero test coverage for a component with a known timer-identity bug and an imperative `defineExpose` channel.
missed.proof: No `.test.ts` or `.spec.ts` anywhere in the repo references `ActionFeedback` or `feedback-chip` (searched the full tree excluding node_modules). The L-4 clock bug, the C#2 unmount leak and the C#6a empty-message path are all unit-testable in isolation — mount with `visible=false`, flip true, flip message while true, assert the emit lands at 2500 ms from the SECOND verdict. The corpus prescribes "a monotonic result ID and cancellable timer are mandatory before implementation closure" (challenge-C-implementation.md:18) without noting there is no test to make that closure mean anything.

unproven: The exact served contrast ratios behind the two MAJOR colour findings. I derived them from token bytes (glass-ui dist/styles/tokens/color-radius.css + dark-arm.css, demo/styles/foundation.css:328) plus standard sRGB alpha compositing and the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula; browser oklch→sRGB gamut mapping and `color-mix(in oklab)` rounding can move the third decimal. The margin is not close (2.31 / 2.78 / 3.27 against a 4.5:1 requirement), so the verdicts are not in doubt, but a live getComputedStyle probe on a mounted chip in both schemes would pin the exact numbers and should be run before the fix is specified.

Whether an `aria-live` attribute placed on the `v-if`-gated node would actually announce. Standard guidance is that a live region must be present in the accessibility tree BEFORE its content changes; ActionFeedback.vue:3-5 mounts the region and its text in the same tick. Whether each browser/AT pair honours a region inserted already-populated is empirical and varies. This matters because it determines whether D#2's cure is a one-attribute change or requires an always-mounted, always-empty region in PaletteCard — do not let the fix ship on the assumption that the one-liner works.

Whether the 2.5 rem max-height clip is reached at the shipped mobile breakpoints. The wrap threshold depends on the real card inner width, which I did not measure. The arithmetic (28 px one line / 44 px two lines against a 40 px cap) is exact; only the wrap point is unmeasured.

D#4's "exceed the viewport" limb at specific viewports — the overflow mechanism is proven from bytes (no min-w-0/break-words, card refuses to clip) but the visible consequence at a given width is not.

L-3b's runtime behaviour (that `showFeedback` on a retained-dead instance throws nothing and logs nothing) rests on the r2's probe, evidence-r2/af-L-r2-registry-leak.mjs, which I did not re-run. The source-level mechanism — the `el &&` guard swallowing Vue's null-on-unmount ref call at BrowsePane.vue:94 / PalettesPane.vue:84 — is dispositive on its own, so the finding stands regardless; only the exact observed symptom is second-hand.
superlatives: The scoped style block is a model of the correct division of labour, and it is the strongest 8 lines in the file. ActionFeedback.vue:50-57 sets ONLY three family geometry custom properties and declares no duration, no easing, no keyframe and no reduced-motion branch — the choreography stays in demo/styles/animations.css:141-166 on six producer tokens. It also states its own reasoning: "scale stays 1 so the row never jitters horizontally" (:52). Local geometry, producer choreography. This is exactly the pattern that twelve of the 46 report-authored files mistook for an ABSENCE of reduced-motion design (codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:175-179, :214-217) — the component is well-built precisely where the corpus graded it red.

The dependency direction is a pure sink and cannot be broken from above. ActionFeedback.vue:20-21 are the file's only two imports, both external (`vue`, `@lucide/vue`); there are zero relative imports in 58 lines — no reach into `../`, into the palette domain, into a composable, or into a sibling. It cannot participate in a cycle. Verified independently; first recorded at challenge-L-library-r2.md:227-229, where the r2 also correctly observes that r1's finding #9 documented this same property while presenting it as a fault.

The barrel discipline around this leaf is right, and states its own reasoning in-file. demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:1-9 uses NAMED re-exports only and names the invariant (PI-6: an SFC's scoped `<style>` is a side-effecting import, so a star re-export defeats per-consumer tree-shaking), and ActionFeedback is deliberately NOT among the six exported symbols — a true internal, correctly hidden. The intent of the seam is correct; only its lint enforcement rotted (confirmed L-2). Recorded at challenge-L-library-r2.md:235-237.

The error rung proves the token idiom is known in-file, one line below the line that abandons it — which is what makes L-1 a one-line change rather than a migration. ActionFeedback.vue:9 `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` resolves byte-exactly to `--destructive` (challenge-L-library-r2.md:239-241). Carried with a caveat: this superlative was measured in light mode only, and in dark mode the same pair is the lowest-contrast reading in the component at 2.78:1 — so it is a superlative of OWNERSHIP, not of legibility, and should not be cited as the template for the success rung without an ink-rung fix.

challenge-L-library-r2.md is the best document in this corpus and should be the template for the remaining re-proofs. It re-tried all eight r1 claims against live bytes and refuted four of its own axis's findings (:21); it corrected the prior provenance audit's MECHANISM while upholding its conclusion (:69 — "the refutation stands; the mechanism cited for it was wrong"), which is a rare and expensive kind of honesty; it scoped L-1 DOWN rather than inflating it (:110); it distinguished a singleton fork from a duplicate and drew the routing consequence (:77); and it rejected the producer primitive that was merely nearest in name in favour of reasoning about placement (:79-83). Its receipt discipline — byte-exact SHA, five re-runnable probes each printing its own falsifier, per-finding witness images — is the standard the REPORT-AUTHORED files (HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:255-257, 0 probes each) conspicuously lack. Its blind spot is absolute contrast, and it is a blind spot precisely because it stayed disciplined about its own axis.

PalettesPane.vue:201-204 is the one place in the whole imperative channel where the addressing hazard was reasoned about explicitly: "K-PALID: the feedback card is registered under the local store key; a palette with no local `id` has no card to address." It is the correct instinct — an author noticing that the registry key and the entity identity can diverge — applied to the one divergence that is visible at compile time. The L-3 hazard (a key that is present but points at a corpse) is the same instinct's blind side, and this comment is evidence the team is one step from seeing it.

killed.claim: BLOCKER — "Double-click Approve double-POSTs AND renders the same proposal twice": two array entries with the same id, a duplicate v-for key, and a downstream single-DELETE that removes both phantom rows.
killed.refutation: The duplicate-state half is unreachable in the live system; only the double-POST half survives, and it is already C-4. Chain: (1) api/src/modules/admin/service/colors.ts:93-98 — `approveColor` calls `transitionStatus(objectId, "proposed", "approved")` and `if (!ok) throw new NotFoundError("Proposed name not found or already processed")`. (2) api/src/modules/color/repository/proposedName.ts:69-80 — the transition is `updateOne({_id: id, status: from}, …)` returning `matchedCount > 0`; MongoDB single-document updates are atomic, so of two concurrent POSTs exactly one can match `status:"proposed"`. (3) demo/platform/transport/client.ts:152-153 — `adminRequest` does `if (!res.ok) throw await ApiProblem.from(res)`, so the losing call REJECTS. (4) demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:71-78 — the append at :75 is inside the `try`, so a rejected second call never appends. The probe manufactured the result: probe-C-queue.test.ts:20-26 mocks `approveColorName: async (_t, id) => { approveCalls.push(id); await sleep(25); }` — it always resolves and never models the 404. The mount probe's "rows rendered for ONE unique id = 2" (challenge-C-implementation.md:120) proves only that Vue renders two elements when handed two identical items, which is not evidence the state can reach that. `rejectColor` (colors.ts:102-113) and `deleteColorName` (colors.ts:80-83, `if (deleted === 0) throw NotFoundError`) are guarded identically. Residual real defect: a double-click fires a second request that 404s and dies in a console.warn — MINOR, and already filed as C-4. The BLOCKER ranking at challenge-C-implementation.md:603-606 ("the only finding that corrupts state the operator cannot repair from the UI") does not stand.

The action buttons measure 28px × 30px and therefore pass; e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:46-56 asserts `undersized` is empty for every admin view and is green. Rendering pending rows adds zero to the REPORT count the finding cites. (The 44px comfort floor D-2 argues for elsewhere is a different, unenforced standard — the finding conflates the two.) The core of D-2 — irreversible opposite-valence commands 6px apart with no confirmation — is confirmed.

killed.claim: "liveRegions: 0 ← nothing announced" / "aria-live = 0 across the whole panel" / "a screen-reader user gets literally nothing".
killed.refutation: The measurement counted `[aria-live]` attributes only and missed the implicit regions the tree actually ships. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:17 puts `role="alert"` on the error plate — an implicit `aria-live="assertive"` region — and :28 puts `role="status"` on the empty plate; AdminListSkeleton.vue:10 adds three more `role="status"` regions. Since the error branch is created asynchronously (after the ~2s load rejection), its insertion IS announced. The narrower claim survives and is what should be carried: a repeat Retry re-renders byte-identical text inside an already-present alert, so no second announcement fires — which is C-7's real defect, not an absence of live regions.

killed.claim: "Reduced-motion behaviour is unproven (route absent from shots/reduced-motion-desktop/)."
killed.refutation: Not unproven — settled, and settled in the tree's favour. docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §1 measures both served guards (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 and glass-ui a11y-overrides.css:1) and establishes that under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the transition-property list is rewritten wholesale to `opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow` — `transform`, and with it the indicator's `translate`/`width`/`height` legs, are removed from the transition set entirely, not merely shortened. The 440ms layout-property transition D-16 flags cannot run under `reduce`. (No M-xx row in the quarantine names AdminNamesPanel, so nothing here is carried against the quarantine's FALSE list; the §1 guard measurement is what applies.)

killed.claim: "`demo/palettes/browser/index.ts` re-exports **22 named symbols** across six sub-barrels."
killed.refutation: It re-exports 20: card 6 (PaletteCard, PaletteCardGrid, PaletteCardSkeleton, ShadowPalette, PaletteColorStrip, CurrentPaletteEditor, :18-25), admin 5 (:27-33), search 3 (:35), dialog 4 (:37-42), slug 1 (:44), status 1 (:46). missed.claim: Three contradictory data-ownership conventions coexist inside one nine-file directory — and that split, not an absent atom, is the mechanism behind the missing pagination.
missed.proof: AdminAuditPanel.vue:107-125, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:138-152 and AdminTagsPanel.vue:113-125 are self-loading containers: each does `inject(ADMIN_PORT_KEY)` + `onMounted(() => …load())`, owns its own filters, and owns its own `PaginationBar` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:83, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126). AdminNamesPanel.vue:132-149 is pure props/emits with its loads fired from the app-root boot layer (demo/color-picker/composables/usePaletteWiring.ts:148-155 eagerly fires both loaders on view entry). AdminUsersPanel.vue:200-234 is a hybrid — it declares props at :212-218 AND injects ADMIN_PORT_KEY at :234. The two prop-driven panels are exactly the two with no pagination; the three container panels all have it. L-6 saw the duplicated state ladder and L-7/D-10 saw the missing PaginationBar, but no axis named the architectural split that produces both — which means the prescribed cures (an `AsyncList` atom, a `<PaginationBar>` insertion) would be grafted onto a cluster that still has no single answer to "who owns the load".

missed.claim: The panel truncates the very string it is asking the moderator to judge, with no full-text affordance — and the repo's own fixture seeds the case that proves it.
missed.proof: AdminNamesPanel.vue:50 renders `{{ item.name }}` inside `class="text-small font-medium truncate"` with no `title`, no tooltip, no expand and no wrap — `grep -c "title=" demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminNamesPanel.vue` → 0. The content column is `flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-hidden` (AdminListItem.vue:17) inside a 512px card at desktop and ~330px at 390px. e2e/smoke/admin/fixtures/admin-populated.ts:93 deliberately seeds a 100-character proposed name ("A Very Long Proposed Color Name That Stresses The Row Min-Width Chain Well Past Any Phone Viewport") as the min-width stressor. The result is that the approve button at :55 commits a decision on a string the reviewer physically cannot read. All three axes recorded truncation as a designed success — challenge-D-design.md:157 lists "truncated | ✅ `truncate` on both lines" in its state table, and challenge-L-library.md:857-859 credits the min-w-0 chain as "a genuine, correctly-diagnosed cure". The min-w-0 chain IS correct; what it cures is layout, and no one asked what the truncation costs a review instrument.

missed.claim: The two loaders have no in-flight guard, no abort and no request sequencing, so overlapping loads resolve last-writer-wins and the shared boolean loading flag is cleared by whichever finishes first.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:35-49 and :51-66 each set a bare `loading*.value = true`, `await`, and clear it in `finally`. There is no in-flight check, no AbortController and no request token. usePaletteWiring.ts:148-155 fires both on view entry `{ immediate: true }`; AdminNamesPanel.vue:37/:87 lets the operator fire either again at any moment; nothing debounces or coalesces. Two overlapping `loadColorQueue` calls both assign `adminColorQueue.value = res.data` in completion order, not issue order, and the first `finally` sets `loadingColorQueue = false` while the second request is still open — so the skeletons vanish mid-flight and a stale page can overwrite a fresh one. C-7 examined Retry only through the latch, never through concurrency; C-1 examined the mutation path's missing guard but not the read path's.

missed.claim: `catch (e: any)` at all five sites erases the typed error hierarchy the transport deliberately ships — this is the type-level root of the untyped error channel L-9 and C-6 describe as a design choice.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useColorNameQueue.ts:43, :60, :76, :87, :99 — five `catch (e: any)`. The repo runs strict TS (tsconfig.base.json), where an unannotated catch binding is `unknown`; the explicit `: any` is a deliberate opt-out. The transport ships three distinct, discriminable classes precisely so callers can triage: `DevMisconfigError` (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:136-142), `ApiUnavailableError`, and `ApiProblem` (thrown at client.ts:125 and :153). Every one is flattened to `e?.message` at the first catch, before `queueLoadError` is even assigned — so L-9's cure ("a discriminated LoadError in demo/platform/transport/") is proposing to build what already exists upstream and is being discarded at this exact line. The correct fix is five `catch (e: unknown)` plus `instanceof` dispatch, not a new type.

missed.claim: The role-less labelled loading wrapper is a six-site cluster family with exactly one correct instance; every axis scoped it to this file, so the prescribed cure would fix one of six.
missed.proof: The same construct — a bare `<div v-if="loading…" class="grid gap-…" aria-label="Loading …">` with no role, wrapping N `role="status"` skeletons — appears at AdminNamesPanel.vue:26 and :76, AdminAuditPanel.vue:36, AdminUsersPanel.vue:46 and :135, and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16. superlatives: The `min-w-0` chain is a genuinely excellent, correctly-diagnosed structural cure, and the comment that carries it is honest engineering prose: AdminNamesPanel.vue:2-12 explains that the old TabsContent grid item sat at `min-width:auto` so un-breakable truncate spans propagated their full-line min-content up as the grid track floor, pushing approve/reject ~250px off-card at 390px. The cure is applied at every link — :13, :24, :43, :75, :93 plus AdminListItem.vue:11 and :17 — and it is fenced by a real test, e2e/smoke/admin/admin-populated.spec.ts:73-81, which asserts `toBeInViewport({ ratio: 1 })` on every action button against a deliberately seeded 100-char stressor (fixtures/admin-populated.ts:90-95). Diagnosis, cure, comment and fence, all four present. That is rare.

`demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue` is the best-designed module anywhere in this component's dependency graph. Its two species are separated at the ARIA layer, not just visually — `role="alert"` on the error branch (:17) and `role="status"` on the empty branch (:28) — and the header comment (:2-13) states the ratified rule ("loading ≠ empty, error ≠ empty") together with the owner rulings that shaped each register (Q6 on the eyebrow, R12/t33-audit-08 on the ghost trio). The scoped `.plate-ink` block (:94-104) documents the measured contrast failure it cures (3.84:1 against a 4.5:1 floor) and why the fix lands on `--ink-muted` rather than an alpha. Twelve consumers inherit all of it.

Per-item accessible names on every action, done properly: AdminNamesPanel.vue:55 `:aria-label="`Approve color name ${item.name}`"`, :65 the same for Reject, :110 for Delete, each paired with `aria-hidden="true"` on the glyph (:56, :68, :113). These are not decorative — e2e/smoke/admin/flows/color-approve.spec.ts:33-35 selects by that exact accessible name, and e2e/smoke/admin/a11y-authed-admin.spec.ts:46-53 gates on zero nameless controls. `AdminListItem.vue` is a textbook atom: 24 lines, three named slots (swatch/content/actions), zero data knowledge, zero props, zero emits. It is the one piece of this cluster that could be lifted into a design system unchanged.

killed.claim: C-3: '`colorSpaceInfo` has **10** keys (`rgb hsl hsv hwb lab lch oklab oklch xyz kelvin`; `grep -c industries` → 14 records, 10 space entries). The other **7** silently render RGB's dossier.' (challenge-C-implementation.md:165-167)
killed.refutation: REFUTED by enumeration. demo/color-session/colorSpaceInfo.ts has 13 keys, not 10 — C omitted `ictcp` (:261), `jzazbz` (:287) and `hex` (:313). `grep -c industries` returns 14 because 13 entries carry the field and the header comment at :4 mentions it — so 14 minus 1 comment = 13 entries, not 10. The masked set is therefore 5 spaces (srgb-linear, display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020), not 7. C-3's own C-2 sibling correctly lists 7 for the MARKDOWN table and C-3 appears to have carried that number across. The defect is real (see confirmed L-1); its stated blast radius is 40% too large, and its claim that ictcp/jzazbz render RGB's facts is false.

killed.claim: D-9: lists four rendered rows as proof the pane 'lies' about Display P3 — 'Components: Red / Green / Blue, 0 to 1' and 'Key Properties: Perceptual Uniformity No, Hue Linearity No, Lightness Separation No' among them (challenge-D-design.md:405-407).
killed.refutation: Two of the four cited bullets are TRUE of Display P3 and cannot carry the 'lie' claim. (a) Components: the range row does not come from the fallback at all — ColorNutritionLabel.vue:217-230 builds `formattedRange` from `PICKER_CHANNELS[resolveColorSpace(space)]`, which is compiler-total over all 17 SpaceIds (picker-color.ts:52-70), so display-p3's `0 to 1` r/g/b ranges are the space's OWN correct values; only the channel NAMES fall back, and `Red/Green/Blue` is correct for display-p3, a98-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020 and srgb-linear alike. (b) Key Properties: Display P3 is not perceptually uniform, is not hue-linear and has no lightness separation — all three 'No' answers are true. The defect survives on `whitePoint` ('Varies (typically D65)' vs fixed D65), `gamut` ('Limited (device-specific)' vs a standardized wide gamut), `created` ('1931' vs 2015/1998) and the Conversion Graph — which is what the tracked frame shows. Same correction applies to C-3's table row 1 ('Definition: additive mixture of red, green and blue light'), which is also true of Display P3.

The scope defect is real and MAJOR; 'destroys the entire application' is not what the source does.

killed.claim: C-10: 'the module table is rebuilt on every mount… The pane is `defineAsyncComponent`-mounted and **re-created on every view switch** (`usePaneRouter.ts:69`).' (challenge-C-implementation.md:394-401)

killed.claim: D-14: '`Markdown.vue:124` `transition: color …` and `ColorNutritionLabel.vue:105` `transition-colors` … are **time-based and ungated**' (challenge-D-design.md:621-623).

D's own grep (zero PRM blocks under demo/scenes/about/) is accurate and I reproduce it — but the correct reading is the one motion-quarantine states for the whole corpus: motion is governed centrally by design, which is the right architecture, not a gap. (Line drift also: the cited `Markdown.vue:124` is live :125; `ColorNutritionLabel.vue:105` is inside a comment block, the `transition-colors` is at :110.) The skeleton-shape limb of D-14 stands.

killed.claim: L-5 INFO: the stale installed `node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js` 'is load-bearing but currently correct… the historical prefix-rewrite bug documented at `vite.config.ts:36-46` is exactly the failure mode where this stale copy would be served silently'; premise: 'glass-ui@7 declares `@mkbabb/value.js:^4.0.0` as a peer' and the demo aliases the bare specifier (challenge-L-library.md:336).
killed.refutation: The staleness fact is real (node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js/dist/subpaths/css.d.ts is Jul 17 21:10; dist/subpaths/css.d.ts is Jul 29 13:48; the peer dep is confirmed in glass-ui's package.json). The risk model is not. glass-ui 7.0.0's shipped dist imports ONLY subpaths — `grep -rho '@mkbabb/value\.js[a-z/.]*' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns exactly `/color` ×7, `/css` ×4, `/easing` ×2 and NO bare specifier. All three hit `valueJsSelfAlias` (vite.config.ts:37-51), which is generated from `package.json#exports` and therefore aliases them to the LOCAL freshly-built `dist/subpaths/*.js`. missed.claim: MISS-1 — `useMarkdownColors` throws from inside a `computed` that is bound directly into the render, giving a SECOND independent path to the same whole-grid ErrorBoundary blowout C-1 books for the dynamic import — and its error posture is self-inconsistent eight lines apart.

That computed is consumed at Markdown.vue:15 `<div … class="markdown-wrapper" :style="mdColorVars">`, so evaluation happens during render; a throw there is caught by the same single ErrorBoundary at App.vue:50…:140 and replaces both panes. The `none` limb is not hypothetical by construction: `Channel = number | "none"` (src/color/model.ts:8); `src/color/operations.ts:38` WRITES `"none"` into the hue slot for powerless colors; and demo/color-session/valueDomain.ts:22-23 documents as law that 'non-finite components pass through untouched (CSS `none` = NaN propagates through conversions per CSS Color 4)' — i.e. the demo's single write gate is designed to carry `none` channels into the model, and `cssColor` is a straight `serializePickerColor(model.value.color)` (useColorPipeline.ts:102). The same function DEGRADES gracefully for `H === "none"` at :52-53 ('A powerless color has no hue to intensify') while THROWING for L or C — one function, two opposite postures. All three axes read this file (L-7 cites :39 for the alpha discard, C-9 cites :33-88 for the recompute chain) and none of them saw the throws. Live reachability of the L/C limb via a `none`-bearing deep link is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE; the throw sites, the render binding and the boundary scope are all source-confirmed.

missed.claim: MISS-2 — the widest type hole in the About subtree is in the barrel, not the component: `DocModule` erases the entire markdown render path to `any`.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/about/markdown/index.ts:3 `export type DocModule = () => Promise<{ default: any }>;`. It flows: AboutPane.vue:70 `import type { DocModule }` → :81 `Record<MarkdownSpace, DocModule>` → Markdown.vue:44-48 `module: DocModule` → :55 `ref<Awaited<ReturnType<DocModule>> | null>` → :64-67 `markdownContent` computed, typed `any` → :16 `<component :is="markdownContent" />`. In a `strict: true` / `verbatimModuleSyntax` / `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` / `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` program (tsconfig.base.json) this is a declared `any` at the type level, which is strictly worse than a cast because no call site can see it. L-10 calls the `(colorSpace: any)` handler 'the second type hole in a 100-line file' and C-2/D-17 count the same two — none of the three axes read the barrel. The honest count for the About closure is at least seven: AboutPane.vue:25, :97; markdown/index.ts:3; ColorNutritionLabel.vue:111 (`path as any`), :123 (`space as string`), :160 (`industries as any`), :213 (`space as keyof typeof colorSpaceInfo`).

missed.claim: MISS-3 — the corpus's shared cure (make `colorSpaceInfo` total over `DisplayColorSpace`) is under-scoped: a SECOND consumer of the same partial table casts it to `any` in a different feature tree.
missed.proof: demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ConsoleRail.vue:172-181 — `const info = (colorSpaceInfo as any)[space]; if (!info?.components) return component;`. L-3's census (challenge-L-library.md:214-219) enumerates four tables and their totality mechanisms but stops at AboutPane's consumers; C-3's cure ('`colorSpaceInfo` must be `Record<DisplayColorSpace, SpaceInfo>`') and D-9's ('the five holes are compile errors') would both break this call site, which nobody costed. It also matters for the *shape* of the cure: unlike ColorNutritionLabel.vue:210-215 this consumer degrades honestly (falls back to the raw channel key rather than substituting another space's data), so it is the exemplar the About site should have copied — a fact worth carrying into the remediation rather than discovering during it.

missed.claim: MISS-4 — `TooltipProvider` is instantiated inside the `v-for`, one shared-context provider per tooltip, and the content it provides is empty.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/about/ColorNutritionLabel.vue:97-142: `<TooltipProvider v-for="(path, index) in currentColorSpaceInfo.conversions" :key="index" :delay-duration="100">` wrapping a single `<Tooltip>` each, and `:139-140` `<TooltipContent class="contents w-64 p-2 text-small"></TooltipContent>` — no children at all. A tooltip Provider is a context root whose whole job is to share `delayDuration`/`skipDelayDuration` state ACROSS sibling tooltips; instantiating N of them defeats the grouping it exists for and is a producer-contract misuse, not a styling choice. Separately, `class="contents"` sets `display: contents` on an absolutely-positioned popper element. D-1 counts these as four 'false triggers' from the composition side and gets the count right, but no axis names the API misuse or the empty content as a code defect — and the empty `<TooltipContent>` is the one item in D-1's list that is unambiguously dead code rather than an open design row.

L-4's negative proof N-4 ('No god modules in the closure') measures module SIZE across the closure but never audits export reachability, and L's §1 import trace walks inbound edges only. missed.claim: MISS-6 — a type-level module cycle inside the About scene: the barrel exports the component that imports its type back from the barrel.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/about/markdown/index.ts:1 `export { default as Markdown } from "./Markdown.vue";` and :3 `export type DocModule = …`; demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:40 `import type { DocModule } from "./";`. `verbatimModuleSyntax` elides the type-only edge, so there is no runtime cycle — but L-9 files the assets/docs↔katex cycle as a MAJOR structural finding and misses this one two directories away. The cure is the same shape as L-9's: `DocModule` belongs in a types module the barrel and the component both import, not in the barrel that re-exports its consumer.

missed.claim: MISS-7 — `tsconfig.demo.json`'s comment block carries a SECOND false statement that L-5 audits past: it claims glass-ui's dist imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier and that `vite.config.ts` mirrors an alias for it. Neither is true at HEAD, and the second cannot be true by construction.
missed.proof: tsconfig.demo.json:20-24 states 'glass-ui's published `dist/` imports the value.js core by the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (aurora/color paths, inv-K-2); a package never installs itself, so the demo aliases that specifier to value.js's own published `dist/value.js` (mirroring the Vite alias in `vite.config.ts`)'. (a) glass-ui 7.0.0's dist imports only subpaths — `/color` ×7, `/css` ×4, `/easing` ×2, zero bare. (b) The mirrored Vite alias does not and cannot exist: vite.config.ts:41-51 builds `valueJsSelfAlias` by mapping `Object.entries(VALUE_JS_PKG.exports)`, and `package.json#exports` has no `"."` key, so no bare-specifier alias is ever emitted. This is the actual reason the `"@mkbabb/value.js": ["./dist/index.d.ts"]` paths entry (:42) is inert — it serves a consumer that no longer exists, mirrors an alias that was never generated, and points at a file that is absent. L-5 caught the '8 public keys' falsehood in the same comment header (:4-7) and missed this one twelve lines below it.

superlatives: `demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:52-70` and `:72-90` — the repo already owns the exact totality mechanism the defective tables lack, one module away from them: `PICKER_CHANNELS` closes `} satisfies Record<SpaceId, readonly ChannelMeta[]>` and `PICKER_SPACE_NAMES` is `Readonly<Record<SpaceId, string>>`. Both are complete over all 17 spaces because the compiler enforces it. This is why L-1's and L-2's cures cost zero invention — and it is the single best argument in the whole corpus.

`demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:1-87` — a genuinely first-class boundary, rare in any codebase: `role="alert" aria-live="assertive"` (:19-20), `tabindex="-1"` plus `nextTick(() => alertRef.value?.focus())` so the SR/keyboard user LANDS on the recovery (:21, :64), a real `<Button>` rather than a dead end (:30-33), `return false` to stop propagation to the app root (:68), and a `reset()` that actually re-renders the subtree (:71-75). The header comment cites WCAG 4.1.3 and 2.4.3 by number. C-1's finding is a scope defect against an excellent instrument, not a missing one.

`demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:31-38` — `pattern.lastIndex = 0` on BOTH sides of `pattern.test()` inside `acceptNode`, with a comment naming the exact failure ('neither an accept nor a reject leaves a stale offset that skips the next text node's first match') and the finding id that produced it. Stateful-`/g/`-regex-inside-a-predicate is one of the most-missed bugs in JavaScript; this is the textbook cure, documented.

`demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:291-306` — the `:has(> .katex-display)` block. The comment states the wrong structure, the true structure, the reason the former selector could never match (`<Katex displayMode>` renders `div.inline-block > span.katex-display > span.katex`, so a direct-child test on `.katex` failed), and the user-visible symptom chain that followed (dead scroll container → wide L*a*b* row clipping at the card edge with content loss). L's negative proof N-2 re-measured it and found it sound; I confirm the source is exactly as described.

`demo/scenes/about/katex/Katex.vue:8-19` — the finest forensic comment in the subtree: a `@import` inside `<style scoped>` was suffixed with the component's `data-v` attribute, so 'all 231 rules matched NOTHING', producing body-sans math, a doubled visible MathML layer, and a 6400px stretchy brace. Cured at the root (script-side import, unscopeable by construction). `throwOnError: false` at :34 is the right failure posture for user-authored math.

`demo/scenes/about/ColorNutritionLabel.vue:190-208` — the fg/bg double-duty split. One `nodeHighlightColor` was serving both a foreground-certified role and a background fill, leaving fixed `--foreground` uncertified on top at a measured 1.57:1. The cure splits the roles honestly: `componentInk` certifies against the RESTING plate's own composited lightness (`useSafeAccentFn("resting")`), and `nodeInk` derives from the FILL's luminance via `contrastInkFor` — a pass by construction, with an explicit empty-string→inherit path on parse failure. killed.refutation: REFUTED BY CONSTRUCTION. AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:47 reads `class="rounded-md border border-card-edge overflow-hidden"`. Per CSS Sizing 3 §5.2, a flex/grid item's automatic minimum size is the content-based minimum ONLY where the item's computed `overflow` in that axis is `visible`; with any other value it is ZERO. `overflow: hidden` therefore already discharges precisely what `min-w-0` discharges. AdminListItem.vue:11 needed the explicit `min-w-0` exactly because it has NO overflow property (`flex items-center gap-3 px-3 py-2.5 rounded-md border border-card-edge min-w-0`). The inner content column is separately protected at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:61 (`flex flex-col gap-0.5 min-w-0 flex-1`), so the truncate spans at :65/:76 cannot propagate a min-content floor either. The row CANNOT blow the track. The axis's stated fact (no literal `min-w-0` class) is true and inert; the stated consequence — the sentence the axis explicitly promotes out of HYPOTHESIS to "a fact" — is false. This is arguably a superlative misread as a defect.

killed.claim: "`:52` `-space-x-1` then overlaps them, so the 5th disc is partly hidden behind the 4th" (challenge-D-design.md:537).

Tailwind v4.3.0 (node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/lib.mjs, the `"space-x"` utility definition) compiles to `:where(& > :not(:last-child)) { --tw-space-x-reverse: 0; margin-inline-start: calc(V * var(--tw-space-x-reverse)); margin-inline-end: calc(V * calc(1 - var(--tw-space-x-reverse))) }` — i.e. a NEGATIVE `margin-inline-end` on every disc except the last, which pulls each disc's SUCCESSOR onto it. The successor is a later sibling, non-positioned, in normal flow, so it paints ON TOP. Disc 5 is fully visible and disc 1 is the most occluded — the exact inverse of the claim. (The truncation and residue-mark half of D-21 survives and is confirmed separately.)

missed.proof: LIVE AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:90 `class="h-7 px-2 text-caption font-display"`. `.text-caption { font-size: var(--type-caption) }` (glass-ui dist/styles/components.css) and `--type-caption: clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)` — viewport-fluid only, never multiplied by `--ui-scale`. The producer's control rung is different by design: dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1 `--control-text-sm: calc(var(--type-caption) * var(--ui-scale))`, applied by dist/components/button/styles.css `.button[data-size="xs"] { … font-size: var(--control-text-sm) }`. dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css `@media (pointer: coarse) { :root { --ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5); --control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem) } }`. So on a phone the Dismiss box goes to 54px tall (the same override D-7 diagnosed and I measured at ≈27×54 in shots/safari-mobile-light/admin-flagged.png) while its label stays pinned at the fine-pointer caption size — a 1.5× legibility gap that `size="xs"` would have closed for free. D-7 found the height arm of this override and missed the type arm; D-13 found the family violation and missed the scale; D-15 found the same scaling distinction on Badge and did not carry it to the Button. The same exemption ripples through `text-mono-caption` (also raw `--type-caption`, glass-ui typography/utilities.css) at :81, :112, :118 and :73.
